messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: service=redis-client-maxclients severity=critical — page fired (see: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD-2026-789)
pagerduty: trigger=rate_threshold, metric=redis.clients.connected, value=10240, threshold=10000
maya: ack — i'm oncall and taking this. paging SREs now :wave:
liam: on it. pulling up grafana and redis INFO. link: https://grafana.internal/d/redis/clients
sarah: seeing massive spike starting ~10:12 UTC. redis-primary-01 connected_clients=10240, maxclients=10000. many short-lived connections from ingestion-worker-*/0
devon: did we have any deploys or backlog jobs? I see a surge of ingestion jobs in k8s: ingestion-worker replicas scaled from 4 -> 20 around 10:06 by autoscaler
maya: ok probable root cause = worker autoscale + no connection pooling in worker. immediate mitigation options:
- throttle ingestion traffic via feature-flag
- temporarily raise redis maxclients (CONFIG SET) and monitor
- reduce worker replicas (scale down)
- enable fallback for non-critical features that hit redis (sessions/analytics)
liam: running quick check: ```bash
redis-cli -h redis-primary-01 INFO clients | grep connected_clients
# -> connected_clients:10240
redis-cli -h redis-primary-01 CONFIG GET maxclients
# -> 1) "maxclients" 2) "10000"
```
sarah: confirmed. errors starting to surface in app logs: `ERR max number of clients reached` for embedding-service and session-store
andre: customer impact: embeddings API calls and realtime session updates failing intermittently -> small subset of users seeing 502/503 on features that rely on redis. ops-monitor shows ~5% error rate spike
maya: action plan (short term, <30m):
1) flip ingestion throttle flag to reduce new connections from workers (devon)
2) scale ingestion-workers down to stable baseline and switch to pooled client config in next deploy (liam/devon)
3) set redis CONFIG SET maxclients 20000 on replicas and primary, then monitor (sarah)
4) create incident ticket and notify product/support for customer messaging (maya)
devon: flipping flag now. ```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" https://flags.internal/api/v1/flags/ingestion-throttle -d '{"value":true}'
```
devon: flag flipped :white_check_mark: traffic dropping from workers in logs
liam: scaling ingestion-workers to 6 replicas now: `kubectl scale deploy/ingestion-worker --replicas=6 -n prod` — ongoing
sarah: running CONFIG SET on replicas first (to avoid hitting primary):
```bash
redis-cli -h redis-replica-01 CONFIG SET maxclients 20000
redis-cli -h redis-replica-02 CONFIG SET maxclients 20000
```
liam: results: replicas accepted new config. connected_clients on replicas still low, primary still at 10.2k
sarah: will apply to primary in a rolling manner; doing `CLIENT PAUSE` not ideal. applying CONFIG SET now and will restart primary if needed
sarah: `redis-cli -h redis-primary-01 CONFIG SET maxclients 20000` -> OK
sarah: connected_clients still 10240 but new connections accepted, error rate dropping in app logs
maya: good. support notified and ticket created: INC-2026-231. @support please stand by for customer-facing blurb
andre: monitoring latency/ops. token-cost endpoints (embeddings) are critical — set fallback to queue requests if redis errors continue
devon: we've observed bursty retry storms from ingestion-worker; i'm adding a 200ms jitter and backoff in the worker config PR, will push to canary in the morning
liam: temporary mitigation summary posted to #incidents (short msg) and added to ticket. link: https://tickets.internal/INC-2026-231
pagerduty: escalation policy halted — incident acknowledged by maya
incident-bot: remind: next oncall rotation in 35m, please create handoff notes if unresolved
maya: handoff plan: i'll own for next 30m, if we still see >1% error rate at 11:00 UTC i'll escalate to SRE lead @andre. leaving detailed steps in the ticket.
liam: will follow up on worker retry/backoff and pool changes. I'll also open a perf-mode PR to add a connection pool in ingestion-worker
sarah: ongoing monitoring: redis errors back down to baseline, embeddings error rate at 0.8% now, sessions at 0.6% — still watching
devon: rolling back autoscaler burst policy for ingestion-workers until we have connection pooling in place
maya: marking incident state = mitigated for now. will update ticket and do full postmortem if we hit recurrence. thanks team :tada:
liam: +1 to postmortem so we can add guardrails (autoscale caps, pooling, circuit-breaker for redis clients)
andre: agree. add runbook item to prevent unpooled clients in high-scale workers
maya: handing off to liam for follow-up and postmortem writeup. I'm done for this page. closing pagerduty incident in 10m if stable.
liam: ack handoff. I'll own the PM and postmortem. closing thread when PD is closed.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-2026-789 acknowledged by maya at 10:22 UTC
pagerduty: incident status -> acknowledged
